title: मुकुन्द–इन्दिरा नाटकमा धार्मिक अभिव्यञ्जना {Religious expression in the play Mukunda-Indira}
nepali: प्रस्तुत लेखमा सनातन धार्मिक मान्यताका आधारमा बालकृष्ण समद्वारा लिखित मुकुन्द–इन्दिरा नाटकको विवेचना गरिएको छ । कृति विश्लेषणका निम्ति श्रुति, स्मृति लगायत शास्त्रीय ग्रन्थहरूमा उल्लिखित धार्मिक चिन्तनबारे विभिन्न समालोचकद्वारा मीमांसा गरिएका पुस्तकहरू एवं ‘मुकुन्द–इन्दिरा’ नाटकको अध्ययन गरी सैद्धान्तिक अवधारणा तय गरिएको छ । उक्त अवधारणाका आधारमा ‘मुकुन्द–इन्दिरा’ नाटकको विश्लेषण गर्दा परोपकार, कर्तव्य, नैतिक आचरणपूर्ण जीवन, ईश्वरप्रतिको विश्वास, प्रायश्चित्त, प्रेम, भक्ति, पाठपूजा एवं उपासनाको समष्टि स्वरूप नै धर्म हो भन्ने समको धर्मसम्बन्धी दृष्टिकोणको निरूपण गरी नाटकका विभिन्न सन्दर्भसहित विवेचना गरिएको छ । अध्ययन गुणात्मक पद्धतिमा आधारित छ र सामग्रीको विश्लेषण व्याख्यात्मक र विवेचनात्मक विधिमा गरिएको छ । यस नाटकमा जीवनको आधार नै धर्म हो र धर्मको आधार प्रेम हो भन्ने मुख्य विचारलाई नायिका इन्दिराको चरित्रबाट व्यञ्जित गरिएको छ भन्ने यस लेखको निष्कर्ष हो । { This article discusses Bal Krishna Sama's play Mukunda-Indira on the basis of traditional religious beliefs. In the say way, old shruti, smriti, and other traditional literature are used to analyze the work. Mukunda-Indira play analysis is based on religious ideas expressed in many ancient scriptures. The literature reviewed, as examined by many critics prior to this, is regarded the theoretical foundation of the study. Analyzing the Mukunda-Indira play based on these established notions, the study is based on the author Sam's belief that religion is a blend of altruism, duty, moral conduct, faith in God, penance, love, devotion, recitation, and worship. This study, in particular, is based on a qualitative method, and the text is studied using explanatory and critical methods. The major premise of this play is portrayed through the character of the heroine, Indira, who believes that religion is the foundation of life and that religion is the foundation of love. This is the actual conclusion of this article.}
american_english: In the present article, the play Mukunda-Indira written by Balkrishna Sama is examined on the basis of Sanatan religious beliefs. For analyzing the work, a theoretical framework has been established by studying books by various critics analyzing the religious thought mentioned in classical texts including Shruti and Smriti, alongside the play 'Mukunda-Indira'. Analyzing the play 'Mukunda-Indira' on the basis of that framework, Sama's perspective on religion—holding that religion is the composite form of benevolence, duty, a morally upright life, faith in God, penance, love, devotion, ritual recitation, and worship—has been delineated and discussed with various contexts from the play. The study is grounded in a qualitative methodology, and the analysis of materials is carried out through interpretive and critical methods. The conclusion of this article is that the core idea that religion is the very foundation of life and love is the foundation of religion is expressed through the character of the heroine Indira in this play.

informal_english: In the present article, the play Mukunda-Indira written by Balkrishna Sama is examined on the basis of Sanatan religious beliefs. For analysing the work, a proper theoretical framework has been established by studying books by various critics analysing the religious thought mentioned in classical texts including Shruti and Smriti, alongside the play 'Mukunda-Indira'. Analysing the play 'Mukunda-Indira' on the basis of that framework, Sama's perspective on religion—holding that dharma is the composite form of benevolence, duty, a morally upright life, faith in God, penance, love, bhakti, puja and worship—has been delineated and discussed with various contexts from the play. The study is grounded in a qualitative methodology, and the analysis of materials is carried out through interpretive and critical methods. The conclusion of this article is that the core idea that dharma is the very foundation of life and love is the foundation of dharma is expressed through the character of the heroine Indira in this play.
